post-12280.title: Friends of the San Juans Restores Critical Shoreline Habitat at Neck Point, Shaw Island
post-12280.summary: At Neck Point on Shaw Island, crews remove rockfall and old bulkhead remnants that buried a surf smelt and sand lance spawning beach, then nourish 500 feet of shoreline with sand and gravel. Natural sediment now moves again, feeding forage fish, salmon, seabirds and orcas while still protecting the road.

image.caption: Shoreline at Neck Point on Shaw Island

images.caption: Shoreline at Neck Point on Shaw Island

Move the arrow to see before (left photo) and after (right photo) at Neck Point on Shaw Island. Crews removed excess armoring rock that had been burying forage fish spawning habitat and disrupting natural beach processes. Notice the shift from angular quarry rock and boulders to natural mixed sand and gravel substrate—the grain sizes that surf smelt and Pacific sand lance need for successful egg deposition. Today, the east end of the shoreline is fully restored, reconnecting sediment transport, supporting forage fish and salmon, and nourishing the beach in front of the road to protect infrastructure while sustaining habitat.

post-11244.summary: In 2024 Friends marks 45 years, launches a Green Boater pledge, expands immersive education, and negotiates a refinery commitment to avoid new vessel traffic near orcas. post-11199.title: Mullis Center Seniors Swim with Salmon!
post-11199.summary: Twelve Mullis Center seniors put on virtual reality headsets and swim through bull kelp forests, herring schools and spawning salmon in Friends' Immersive Salish Sea Education Program. The program, run for four years in island high schools, now reaches adults and grew youth participation 89 percent this year.

post-12358.title: Tina Whitman | Senior Science Director
post-12358.summary: Tina Whitman, winner of the 2022 Salish Sea Science Prize, is Friends' Senior Science Director and has run its shoreline research, restoration and protection programs since 2002. She serves on the county's Salmon Recovery Technical Advisory Group and lives on Orcas Island, happiest at the beach.

post-11130.title: San Juan County’s Comprehensive Plan Demystified
post-11130.summary: San Juan County's Comprehensive Plan is the roadmap for growth, farmland, forests, water, and a new Climate Element, and state law requires periodic updates. Friends invites islanders to join a Comp Plan Action Team to write letters, testify, and push for policies that keep shorelines and communities resilient.

post-11020.title: Election Season Update
post-11020.summary: Ahead of the 2024 election, Friends explains its nonpartisan role, its Protector Priority Platform, and its board endorsements to renew the county Land Bank and vote no on I-2117. Protecting island shorelines and the Salish Sea depends on county planning and state climate funding.

post-10971.summary: Pediatrician and Coast Guard Auxiliary member Dr. Manny Eusebio models green boating from his sailboat in Bellingham, leaving a clean wake to care for the marine environment. post-10966.summary: Friends hosts a November 2024 screening of FISH WAR at the San Juan Community Theatre in Friday Harbor, marking fifty years since the Boldt Decision affirmed Treaty Tribes' salmon fishing rights. Lummi Blackhawk Dancers open the evening and Tribal leaders discuss sovereignty, stewardship and fisheries.

post-10876.title: Friends Secures Safer Waters for Southern Resident Killer Whales
post-10876.summary: Phillips 66 planned up to 61 new tanker or barge round trips a year around the San Juans to supply its Ferndale sustainable aviation fuel project. post-10840.title: Governor Inslee with Friends
post-10840.summary: Governor Jay Inslee tours the San Juans' kelp and eelgrass beds aboard the Friday Harbor Labs vessel Kittiwake with Friends' staff and orca recovery leaders. He also promotes the Green Boater Pledge from the Port of Friday Harbor Marina to protect these underwater forests.

post-6841.title: Lovel Pratt | Marine Protection and Policy Director
post-6841.summary: Lovel Pratt has directed Friends' marine protection and policy work since 2018, drawing on consulting in maritime shipping and oil spill prevention and a term on San Juan County Council. She represents environmental interests on the Puget Sound Harbor Safety Committee, Cherry Point Aquatic Reserve committee and county Marine Resources Committee.

post-10821.title: Samish Indian Nation and Friends Proactively Planning for the San Juan Islands
post-10821.summary: The Samish Indian Nation and Friends receive $499,000 from NOAA to plan for the San Juan Islands' shorelines as seas rise and erosion and flooding grow. The project maps shoreline armor, eelgrass, kelp, forage fish beaches and cultural resources to build a protection blueprint for the islands.

post-10778.title: Ayn Carrillo Gailey | Lead Ambassador
post-10778.summary: Ayn Carrillo Gailey, lead island ambassador on Orcas, brings a lifelong love of the sea and a talent for collaboration and fundraising to Friends' volunteer team. She helps connect islanders to the work of protecting the Salish Sea and island forests.

images.caption: ayn gailey headshot

post-10752.title: Friends Endorses Renewal of Land Bank
post-10752.summary: Friends' board endorses renewing San Juan County's real estate excise tax, which funds the Conservation Land Bank and affordable housing. The Land Bank conserves shorelines, forests, and farms, and works with Friends to prioritize shoreline protection for salmon recovery.

post-6844.title: Jess Newley | Community Science and Education Director
post-6844.summary: Jess Newley, a SCUBA diver with a master's in environmental education, has led Friends' community science and education programs since 2018. Her work spans student and boater education, Pacific sand lance beach surveys and community science projects that connect islanders to life beneath the surface.

post-10713.title: Protecting People, Nature, and Staying Issue-Centered!
post-10713.summary: Friends explains that it endorses issues, not candidates, and relies on science, education, policy and law to protect the islands and Salish Sea. Ahead of the 2024 elections it previews its Protector Platform and backs the Conservation Land Bank and the Home Fund for affordable housing.

post-10695.summary: Low tides in June and July reveal sea stars, anemones, nudibranchs, and bull kelp along the county's 400 miles of shoreline. post-10691.summary: Orcas Island volunteer Raven Preston has given nearly 30 hours of database and user-experience expertise to help Friends improve its community outreach. She explains why interconnection with nature and a strong sense of place keep her involved in protecting the islands.

post-10679.summary: Representative Rick Larsen meets Friends on San Juan Island and voices support for continued federal funding of eelgrass mapping and other shoreline restoration through the EPA, NOAA and Fish and Wildlife. post-12035.title: Upright Head Beach Restoration (Lopez) – In Progress
post-12035.summary: The Upright Head Beach project on Lopez Island is restoring intertidal habitat by removing concrete debris and shoreline armor. Scheduled for completion in Fall 2026, it aims to improve forage fish spawning grounds and support local marine ecosystems.

post-12028.title: Neck Point Beach Restoration (Shaw) – In Progress
post-12028.summary: Consisting of 500 feet of a documented forage fish spawning site, this beach will be restored through removal of an unnecessary bulkhead as well as a cleanup of intertidal debris. Set to be completed in Fall 2024.

post-12023.title: Eastsound Waterfront Park Beach Restoration (Orcas) – In Progress
post-12023.summary: Friends of the San Juans is supporting ongoing beach restoration at Eastsound Waterfront Park on Orcas Island, improving natural shoreline processes, enhancing habitat for marine species, and increasing long-term coastal resilience.

post-10465.title: Become a Green Boater Today!
post-10465.summary: Friends' Green Boater pledge asks boaters to anchor beyond eelgrass, give whales space and leave a clean wake. Herring spawn on eelgrass in only a few county bays, including Eastsound, West Sound, Blind Bay, Mud Bay and Hunter Bay, so dropping anchor deeper than 25 feet protects the food web that feeds salmon and orcas.

images.caption: white boat docked at the marina

post-10463.title: Diving into eelgrass health
post-10463.summary: Friends, DNR, and Friday Harbor Labs are mapping eelgrass in 21 bays and comparing it to a 2003 survey; last summer showed declines in 12 bays, mostly in shallow water. Eelgrass shelters forage fish and young Chinook, so knowing where it thrives guides protection for salmon and orcas.

post-12360.title: Magali Cota | Staff Attorney and Legal Director
post-12360.summary: Magali Cota serves as Friends' Staff Attorney and Legal Director, drawing on experience with Earthjustice, the Western Environmental Law Center, and Columbia Riverkeeper. She works to protect the islands' environmental integrity and elevate communities most affected by regulatory failures.

post-10285.title: Artists on Yellow Island
post-10285.summary: Nearly forty artists and a Lummi council member join Friends' first Artist Expedition to Yellow Island in April, sketching camas, chocolate lily and shooting star in bloom. Friends invites artists into ongoing collaborations, believing art can move people to protect and restore the islands.

post-10278.title: Gathering of the Eagles
post-10278.summary: Friends is fiscal sponsor for Gathering of the Eagles, an intertribal canoe journey following Lummi ancestral routes through Lopez, San Juan and Orcas Islands in May 2024. Islanders are invited to welcome canoes at Jackson Beach and Olga Dock, share potluck dinners and hear fireside storytelling.

post-6828.title: Ken Carrasco | President
post-6828.summary: Ken Carrasco, a retired marine biologist on Orcas Island, serves as president of Friends' board. His Coast Guard icebreaker service and two years researching the Exxon Valdez spill shaped his conviction about climate change and clean, quiet boating on the Salish Sea.

post-10095.summary: Friends' outreach on Washington's oil-facility financial responsibility rule generates more than 200 public comments, a 27-organization letter, and a Seattle Times op-ed. The rule decides whether refineries and pipelines, not taxpayers, cover the full cost of a major spill.

post-10038.summary: More than 90 percent of waterfront parcels in the San Juans are private homes, so landowners hold the key to healthy shorelines. post-9990.title: Business and Organizations that Show Up for Friends!
post-9990.summary: Friends thanks dozens of local businesses, artists, farms, and organizations that donated goods, space, and time over the past year. Their support helps fund shoreline and Salish Sea protection across the islands.

post-9641.title: Who Foots the Bill for an Oil Spill?
post-9641.summary: Washington's draft rule would require refineries and pipelines to cover only $300 million of a large oil spill, though Ecology estimates such a spill could cost $10.8 billion. Friends urges at least $1 billion per facility and higher amounts for tar sands to protect orcas, salmon, forage fish, and eelgrass.

post-9735.summary: Friends welcomes executive administrator Isabel Alexander and board members Kai Sanburn of Lopez and Tom Reynolds of Brown Island. post-9717.title: Friday Harbor Youth Support Recycling Reform in Olympia

post-9527.title: Legislative Action Alerts!
post-9527.summary: During Washington's 2024 legislative session Friends sends weekly action alerts on bills affecting the islands and Salish Sea, from the ReWrap Act and Right to Repair to petroleum pricing. It opposes bills that would open rural lands to more accessory dwelling units.

post-8745.title: Eva Schulte | Executive Director
post-8745.summary: Eva Schulte leads Friends as executive director, bringing experience from the Whatcom Community College Foundation, the Sierra Club Foundation, and community organizations. She sees solving the climate crisis for people and nature as the central work of protecting the islands.

post-9492.title: Take a stand against big oil in support of the Salish Sea!
post-9492.summary: Phillips 66 rebuilt part of its Ferndale refinery without permits to handle renewable diesel for transshipment, which could add vessel traffic in the Salish Sea. post-9417.title: The Rebirth of a Beach With a Big Impact
post-9417.summary: In November 2023 Friends and landowner Corinne Storey remove a 225-foot creosote retaining wall and fifty truckloads of fill from the west side of Broken Point on Shaw Island, then plant 1,500 dune grasses and native shrubs. post-9405.summary: Friends welcomes a Council of Scientific Advisors: Drew Harvell, who studies eelgrass wasting disease, hydrophone builder Val Veirs, oceanographer Chuck Greene and marine geologist Gary Greene, who mapped the seafloor around the San Juans. post-9512.summary: Pacific herring are small schooling fish that feed salmon, seabirds, seals, and ultimately Southern Resident orcas, and hold deep cultural and economic value. post-9273.title: Friends’ Action Ensures Refinery Project Will Not Impact endangered Orca

post-9129.summary: Friends hosts summer Meet and Mingle gatherings at Madrone Cellars in Friday Harbor, Lum Farm on Orcas and Odlin County Park on Lopez. post-9082.title: Collaborative Eelgrass Research Underway!

post-8533.title: Take Action—Ecology Needs to Hear from You!

post-8152.title: Understanding Ecology’s rulemaking to reduce oil spill risks and impacts
post-8152.summary: Washington moves 10 billion gallons of oil through 12,000 transfers a year, and Ecology's rule update leaves gaps: no seismic standards for older containment and no pre-booming for transfers under 500 gallons per minute. post-13922.title: Important Lessons Learned From an Oil Spill
post-13922.summary: In September 2022 crews raise the fishing vessel Aleutian Isle from 200 feet off the west side of San Juan Island and remove its remaining fuel. post-7438.title: Legal Victory for Friends of the San Juans against Phillips 66 Refinery’s proposal to construct new storage tanks
post-7438.summary: The Washington Court of Appeals rules for Friends in its challenge to Phillips 66's new crude and fuel oil storage tanks at its Ferndale refinery. Because the refinery never quantified added tanker traffic, permit conditions now require annual vessel monitoring so the project does not increase shipping impacts on Southern Resident killer whales.

post-12036.title: West Sound Beach Restoration (Orcas)
post-12036.summary: On Orcas Island's West Sound, a priority forage fish spawning region, landowners moved their house back from the shore so Friends could remove a rock and creosote bulkhead in 2015. Crews hauled out 530 tons of rock and fill, planted 1,600 native trees and shrubs, and restored 150 feet of pocket beach.

post-12034.summary: At Turn Point on San Juan Island, Friends removes 60 cubic yards of unnecessary rock bulkhead from 200 feet of shoreline in 2009, reconnecting a rare salt marsh to the sea. Sand and gravel nourishment restores spawning beach for surf smelt and sand lance and opens habitat for juvenile salmon.

post-12033.title: Thatcher Bay Nearshore Restoration (Blakely)
post-12033.summary: In 2013 Friends and Blakely Island Timberlands remove a log-handling facility, 955 cubic yards of concrete and fill, and over 20 creosote pilings from northern Thatcher Bay, restoring 200 feet of surf smelt spawning beach. A smaller rebuilt barge landing keeps forest access while uncovering 5,000 square feet of intertidal habitat for juvenile Chinook.

post-12032.summary: On Blind Bay, Shaw Island, Friends and San Juan County Public Works shrink the rock footprint protecting Smuggler's Cove Road, pull large rock off the beach and add sand and gravel along 300 feet of a surf smelt spawning beach in 2009. Road armoring is the county's biggest threat to forage fish spawning habitat.

Water now flows freely, summer temperatures drop, and schools of young salmon appear in the five-acre lagoon within months, alongside herring, surf smelt, and shellfish beds.

With 220 native trees and shrubs planted along 430 feet of shore, forage fish and juvenile salmon gain habitat.

post-12029.summary: Friends removes a 55-cubic-yard berm that blocked tidal flow into the Neck Point salt marsh on Shaw Island, restoring channels so high tides flood the marsh and low tides flush it. Salt marshes supply insect prey for juvenile salmon, and fish are now seen using the reopened channels.

The restored beach and marsh feed young Chinook migrating past Sucia.

Tidal water, nutrients, and juvenile fish now move freely between marsh and bay, and 50 native shrubs replace a mowed edge.

post-12021.summary: In 2017 and 2019 Friends and landowners along Blind Bay on Shaw Island remove about 120 cubic yards of armor rock that buried the beach and add sand and gravel fish mix. Surf smelt spawn year-round and herring spawn on eelgrass offshore, so over 1,000 feet of spawning beach across six parcels is restored.

post-13211.title: Buoy Upgrade Program
post-13211.summary: Herring in San Juan County spawn only in a few eelgrass bays, including West Sound, Blind Bay, Garrison Bay, Mud Bay, and Shoal Bay, and their numbers are critically depressed. Friends offers waterfront owners funding and technical help to upgrade or relocate mooring buoys and remove debris so eelgrass and herring can recover.

post-13989.title: BREAKING: Xylene Manufacture and Export in Anacortes Stopped!
post-13989.summary: Marathon Petroleum withdraws plans to make and export 15,000 barrels a day of xylene from its Anacortes refinery, after Friends and five partner groups appeal the permits and reach a settlement. The Salish Sea avoids 120 added tank vessel transits, with their noise and spill risk for Southern Resident orcas.

post-13992.title: Action Alert: Require Whatcom County to Address Philips 66 Project’s Impacts to the Southern Resident Orcas
post-13992.summary: Whatcom County issues a mitigated determination for Phillips 66's new 300,000-barrel crude and 80,000-barrel fuel oil tanks at Ferndale without addressing added tanker traffic, oil spill risk or the Southern Resident killer whales whose critical habitat borders the terminal. Friends asks people to comment by August 2, 2019.

post-13998.title: You did it! All Orca Emergency Response Bills Passed!
post-13998.summary: In 2019 the Washington Legislature passes all five Orca Emergency Response bills, covering oil transportation safety, vessel distance from Southern Residents, whale watching guidelines, toxic pollution, and Chinook abundance. Friends, which co-petitioned for the whales' federal listing in 2001, thanks islanders who contacted their representatives.

post-13994.title: Watch the Video: 3/20 Protect What You Love Orca Event
post-13994.summary: At a March 2019 event in Friday Harbor, Friends and orca researcher Dr. Deborah Giles explain what Southern Resident orcas need to survive, from Chinook salmon to healthy county shorelines. The recording shows how islanders can press elected officials for orca protection and recovery.

post-13561.title: Comment on Canada’s Trans Mountain Pipeline Expansion project by November 20th!
post-13561.summary: Friends asks islanders to comment to Canada's National Energy Board by November 20 against the Trans Mountain expansion, which would route tar sands tankers through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass. A Tsleil-Waututh study finds a 37 percent chance of a large tanker spill over fifty years, which could push Southern Resident orcas toward extinction.

post-13563.title: Good News! Trans Mountain Pipeline Approval Rejected!
post-13563.summary: Canada's Federal Court of Appeal rejects approval of the Trans Mountain pipeline in August 2018 because the government ignored tanker traffic impacts on Southern Resident killer whales and failed to consult First Nations meaningfully. Construction halts, and Friends credits Salish Sea protectors who fought the project since 2013.

post-14000.title: Action Alert: Recent Salish Sea Salmon Spill
post-14000.summary: Up to 305,000 farmed Atlantic salmon escape when a Cooke Aquaculture net pen near Cypress Island breaks apart in 2017, threatening wild Pacific salmon with disease and competition. Friends asks islanders to thank the Governor for a permit moratorium and urge Ecology to block new net pens.

post-11965.summary: In Barlow Bay on Lopez Island, Friends, the Tulalip Tribes, and DNR remove a derelict dock in 2013, including 1,200 square feet of overwater structure, 26 creosote pilings, and 26 cubic yards of rock. The work restores eelgrass and sand lance and surf smelt spawning habitat in Mackaye Harbor, a priority nearshore area.

page-15628.title: Addressing Oil Spill Risk
page-15628.summary: Nearly 12,000 ships crossed the Salish Sea's narrow, rocky shipping lanes in 2025, and more than 2,200 more are expected in 2026 as Canadian crude exports surge. Friends works to cut oil spill risk from tankers, over-water fuel transfers and fishing boats like the Aleutian Isle, which sank near San Juan Island in 2022.

page-15261.summary: Participants in Friends events agree to a liability waiver, assuming the risks of the activity and travel to and from it and releasing Friends and its staff from claims. The agreement is governed by Washington law and notes that Friends provides no medical insurance.

page-14172.title: Our Core Values
page-14172.summary: Friends' five core values are reverence for interconnectedness, advocacy and justice, integrity, courage and steadfastness, and vigilant protection. They guide how the organization works with Tribal Nations, scientists, agencies, and islanders to safeguard the San Juan Islands and the Salish Sea.

page-12742.title: Green Boating
page-12742.summary: Boaters protect the Salish Sea by anchoring in water deeper than 25 feet to spare eelgrass, staying 1,000 yards from Southern Resident orcas, pumping out rather than dumping, and reporting every oil spill. Shoreline owners can help by upgrading mooring buoys and removing derelict docks and creosote pilings.

page-13905.title: Impact Report 2021-2025
page-13905.summary: Friends' 2021 to 2025 impact report tallies 6,000 feet of shoreline restored, 81 mooring buoy upgrades that protect eelgrass, four derelict overwater structures removed from herring spawning areas and $10 million in restoration funding leveraged. It also marks the 1,000-yard orca protection law, two Comprehensive Plan updates and education reaching 2,500 youth and adults.

page-12595.title: Protector Pledge
page-12595.summary: The Protector Pledge invites supporters to commit to a recurring gift through Friends' 50th anniversary in 2029. Steady funding sustains year-round shoreline restoration, wildlife protection and policy advocacy across the San Juan Islands and Salish Sea.

page-11637.title: The Future Through Education
page-11637.summary: Friends' education programs bring the Salish Sea to classrooms and fairs through a mobile learning dome, virtual reality video of eelgrass, kelp, and forage fish, and an open online curriculum. Green Boating training and the Plastic-Free Salish Sea coalition turn that learning into everyday action on the water.

page-8564.title: Youth Education
page-8564.summary: Friends has taught science and conservation in island schools for over 20 years through forage fish beach surveys, virtual reality food web tours, and weekly high school clubs. Students learn about local habitats, visit Olympia to speak with legislators, and join community science and restoration work.

page-11629.title: Shoreline Ecosystems
page-11629.summary: Eroding bluffs build the beaches where surf smelt and sand lance lay eggs, eelgrass meadows shelter young salmon and crabs, and bull kelp forests calm waves and store carbon. Armoring, docks, vegetation clearing and runoff break these processes, so Friends maps habitat, restores beaches and offers free ShoreFriendly site visits to property owners.

page-11895.title: Habitat Restoration
page-11895.summary: Friends' restoration program restores natural beach processes for forage fish, eelgrass and herring by removing bulkheads, derelict docks and creosote pilings and upgrading mooring buoys. Its project list spans the islands, from Upright Head and Shoal Bay on Lopez to West Sound on Orcas, Thatcher Bay on Blakely and Mud Bay on Sucia.

page-13554.title: Species Protection
page-13554.summary: The Salish Sea holds 113 endangered species, and Friends works to protect Southern Resident orcas, Cherry Point herring, Chinook salmon, and the Island Marble butterfly through petitions, safer shipping, and habitat restoration. San Juan beaches and eelgrass supply the forage fish and shelter salmon need on their way to sea.

page-14004.title: Past Salish Sea Protection Projects
page-14004.summary: A timeline of Friends' Salish Sea protection work: rising tanker traffic after the Trans Mountain expansion, lessons from the Aleutian Isle spill off San Juan Island, court wins limiting Phillips 66 vessel traffic, stopping xylene exports from Anacortes, and orca protection bills. Each effort reduces spill and vessel risks to orcas and salmon.

page-11647.title: Partners
page-11647.summary: Friends works alongside Tribes and First Nations, state and county agencies, schools, nonprofits, businesses and regional coalitions to protect the islands and the Salish Sea. The page lists featured partners and the committees Friends serves on, from the Puget Sound Harbor Safety Committee to the county Marine Resources Committee.

page-11631.title: The Salish Sea
page-11631.summary: Friends' Salish Sea program works to keep waters safer, cleaner and quieter for Southern Resident killer whales by fighting shipping pollution, improving oil spill prevention and holding refineries, pipelines and terminals accountable through permitting, rulemaking and litigation. Recent wins include a 1,000-yard orca buffer in state law and 12.6 million gallons of crude shipments avoided.

page-11623.title: Sovereign Nations
page-11623.summary: Friends works as a guest on Northern Straits Salish territory and takes leadership from Sovereign Nations in protecting the islands. With the Samish Indian Nation, it combines mapping of armor, sea level rise, eelgrass, kelp, and forage fish beaches with cultural values to build a shoreline protection blueprint.

page-14058.title: Our Work
page-14058.summary: Friends works in four areas: protecting the Salish Sea from shipping pollution and oil spills, strengthening island communities through land use and water planning, restoring shoreline habitat, and educating people of all ages. Science, relationships, and action come together to keep beaches, wetlands, and nearshore waters healthy.

page-11624.title: Island Communities and Resources
page-11624.summary: Friends, founded in 1979 to help shape San Juan County's first Comprehensive Plan, still reviews every county land-use permit and draft policy to protect farms, forests, freshwater and wild habitat. It helped create the Land Bank, brings islanders into planning decisions and supplies sea level rise data for adapting to a changing climate.

page-10907.title: Protector Platform
page-10907.summary: Friends' Protector Platform lays out priorities for county leaders: good governance, Tribal treaty rights, smart growth, clean energy siting and shoreline protection. It calls for relocating at-risk coastal roads as seas rise, modernizing county docks and buoys, and fixing shoreline permitting, noting over 90 percent of 108 bulkheads built from 2009 to 2019 lacked permits.

page-10567.title: Agricultural Resource Lands and San Juan County’s 2025 Comprehensive Plan
page-10567.summary: Agricultural Resource Land zoning protects large, high-quality farm parcels from subdivision as San Juan County's population heads toward 19,000 by 2036. Friends explains how the designation works and argues the county needs more protected farmland, not less, for food security and rural character.

page-10565.title: Forest Resource Lands and San Juan County’s Comprehensive Plan Update
page-10565.summary: Forest Resource Land zoning keeps island forests in forestry rather than dense development, protecting water quality, aquifer recharge, wildlife habitat, and carbon storage. Since 2000 San Juan County has de-designated 167 acres, and Friends asks residents to tell the Council to designate more forest land in the Comprehensive Plan update.

page-11613.title: More Ways to Help
page-11613.summary: Friends invites supporters to give, volunteer, take action, attend events, subscribe to monthly e-news or leave a planned gift. Every contribution funds the science, restoration and advocacy that protect the San Juan Islands and the Salish Sea for future generations.

page-9560.title: Landowner Resources
page-9560.summary: Waterfront owners in San Juan County can request a free Shore Friendly site visit with a coastal geologist and shoreline biologist, followed by written advice on erosion, flooding, native plants and drainage. More than 450 owners have taken part since 2008, some removing seawalls and later watching surf smelt spawn on their beaches.

page-11334.title: Shore Friendly Contractor Resources
page-11334.summary: Friends gathers presentations and handouts for contractors on shoreline geology, tree care, drainage, weed control, and reducing armor, drawn from its Winter 2025 Shore Friendly workshop. The resources help excavators, arborists, and landscapers build and maintain waterfront property without harming beach habitat.

page-11028.title: I Pledge to…
page-11028.summary: Friends asks members to pledge multi-year support so it can plan larger projects to restore shorelines, study climate effects on the islands, shape public policy and teach the next generation. page-14259.summary: Membership, donations, and planned gifts fund Friends' advocacy, restoration, and education. Over 47 years that support has identified more than 100 forage fish spawning beaches, restored 6,000 feet of shoreline, and brought immersive Salish Sea education to 500 youth.

page-11730.summary: Donations to Friends fund shoreline restoration, legal advocacy, community science, and education across the San Juan Islands. page-10500.title: Green Boating
page-10500.summary: After taking the Green Boater Pledge, boaters can become ambassadors by hanging posters at marinas, joining beach cleanups or hosting a talk at their yacht club. page-9381.title: Friends of the San Juans Whitener Group Training
page-9381.summary: Friends' board commits to completing the Whitener Group's Indian Country 101 and 102 courses by 2024, with each member studying a local Tribe or Nation such as the Samish, Lummi or W̱SÁNEĆ. A reading list of place-based maps, videos and scholarship on Coast Salish fisheries and stewardship supports the learning.

page-10372.title: Take the Green Boater Pledge!
page-10372.summary: Boaters can take the Green Boater Pledge by reviewing Friends' Green Boating Guide, signing online, and picking up a kit at the Friday Harbor office. The pledge commits mariners to practices that protect eelgrass, kelp, and whales from anchors, noise, and pollution.

page-9062.title: Priorities
page-9062.summary: Friends' 2022-2025 strategic priorities focus on new research and restoration projects, expanded K-12 education, climate action, equity, and stronger communications. Milestones include a virtual reality science program, wins for Southern Resident orcas and shoreline restoration, and research into recent eelgrass declines.

page-13754.title: The Little Fish
page-13754.summary: Herring, surf smelt and sand lance feed young salmon in the islands, and Friends found 21 new spawning beaches between 2018 and 2022. But 27 miles of shoreline are armored, most new armor is unpermitted, and eelgrass and kelp are declining, so Friends offers waterfront owners free site visits and restoration help.

page-9771.title: Interactive Tool: Over-Water Oil Transfers
page-9771.summary: In 2023 alone, Class 1 facilities moved nearly 4.5 billion gallons of oil in 2,589 over-water transfer operations to and from vessels. Friends' interactive tool lets people explore these transfers, which exclude pipeline, rail and truck movements.

page-9500.title: Immersive Salish Sea Education
page-9500.summary: Immersive Salish Sea Education offers educators grab-and-go units with 360-degree underwater video, slides, and activities on eelgrass, herring, the marine food web, and the loss of the sunflower star. The free curriculum helps students experience the habitats that sustain island shorelines.

page-7701.summary: Friends offers waterfront landowners free technical help with shoreline vegetation, including site visits, planting plans, and handouts on native plants, noxious weeds, and county rules. page-7445.title: Sea Level Rise Resources for San Juan County
page-7445.summary: Friends gathers sea level rise resources for San Juan County: workshop presentations from Lopez, Orcas and San Juan islands, survey results from 174 attendees, inundation maps for four islands, and a shoreline stewardship guide. page-7401.title: Salish Sea Vessel Traffic Projections
page-7401.summary: Friends' Salish Sea Vessel Traffic Projections, updated in September 2024, track 23 new or expanding terminal and refinery projects that could add at least 2,005 ocean-going transits a year, an 18 percent increase over 2023. The Trans Mountain pipeline expansion and Roberts Bank Terminal 2 account for over 60 percent of the growth.

page-6530.title: Our Story
page-6530.summary: Islanders founded Friends of the San Juans in 1979 to protect the islands' beauty, character and wildness, with early wins including the county's first Comprehensive Plan and stopping large-scale development near Lime Kiln State Park. Friends is a nonpartisan nonprofit that endorses issues, not candidates.
